raw_segments.text: The seine orage in France raises the value of the coin higher than in proportion to the
quantity of pure gold which it contains.
Thus, by the edict of January 1726, the mint price of fine gold of 24 carats was fixed
at 740 livers nine sues and one denier one eleventh the mark of eight Paris ounces.
See Dictionnaire des Moneys, Tom, Roman II, Article Seine Ridge, p. 439, par 81.
Abbot de Basinghen, Consaler commissaire en la Cour des Moneys a Paris.
The gold coin of France, making an allowance for the remedy of the mint, contains 21 carats
and three-fourths of fine gold and two carats one-fourth of alloy.
The mark of standard gold, therefore, is worth no more than about 671 livers ten deniers.
But in France, this mark of standard gold is coined into 30 Louis d'Ores of 24 livers
The coinage, therefore, increases the value of a mark of standard gold bullion by the
difference between 671 livers ten deniers and 720 livers or by 48 livers nineteen sues
